values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Cheniere project page says this 21.5-mile, 48-inch pipeline carries the feed gas that the Corpus Christi liquefaction plant needs to make LNG. An EIA pipeline projects entry says it allows delivery to the Corpus Christi LNG facility.

verifications.note: Page names the Corpus Christi Pipeline and says it transports feed gas required by the Corpus Christi plant to produce LNG.
EIA entry for the Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline Project says it allows delivery to Corpus Christi LNG facility.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already said yes. Added the terminal, a note, and two refs. The two refs come from different publishers.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: An EIA pipeline projects entry describes this 21-mile, 42-inch line as a feed gas pipeline delivering gas to Cheniere's Corpus Christi Stage 3 liquefaction trains. A 2019 Department of Energy environmental assessment covers the Stage 3 project.

verifications.note: EIA entry for the Corpus Christi Stage III Pipeline says it delivers feed gas to the Stage 3 liquefaction trains and lists LNG as the demand served.
Department of Energy environmental assessment for Corpus Christi LNG Stage 3.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already said yes. Added the terminal, a note, and refs. The Department of Energy document is a general Stage 3 assessment, so the EIA entry carries the tie.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission draft environmental impact statement notice from April 2026 lists the compressor stations and meter work on the Creole Trail Pipeline as part of the Sabine Pass Stage 5 Expansion Project. An EIA pipeline projects entry describes the same compressor-only expansion.

verifications.note: Notice names the Creole Trail Pipeline aboveground facilities, Tarpon and Gillis compressor stations, as part of the Sabine Pass Stage 5 liquefaction expansion.
EIA entry for the CTPL Expansion Project describes the compressor-only expansion at Gillis and Tarpon.

records.researcher_notes: New tag. The expansion is part of the Sabine Pass Stage 5 LNG export project. EIA's demand served cell is blank for this entry, so the notice is the main source.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Cheniere project page says the 94-mile, 42-inch bidirectional Creole Trail Pipeline connects the Sabine Pass LNG facility with large interstate pipelines. The facility now exports LNG.

verifications.note: Page says the pipeline is bidirectional and connects the Sabine Pass LNG facility with interstate pipelines.

records.researcher_notes: New tag. The pipeline was built in 2008 for the import terminal, and the page does not say export feed gas in so many words. It serves the Sabine Pass terminal that now exports LNG, so I marked it yes at medium.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Federal Register notice from December 2014 covers the Creole Trail Pipeline Expansion Project together with the Sabine Pass Liquefaction Expansion Project, under dockets CP13-552 and CP13-553. An EIA entry for the 104.3-mile Creole Trail expansion lists LNG as the demand served.

verifications.note: Notice covers the Sabine Pass Liquefaction Expansion Project and the Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline Expansion Project, dockets CP13-552 and CP13-553.
EIA entry for Creole Trail Expansion Project 2, docket CP13-553, lists LNG as demand served and notes it is on hold.

records.researcher_notes: New tag. The project is cancelled, but it was planned to serve the Sabine Pass liquefaction expansion. The notice covers the pair of projects together.
